purpose: Compare stock Codex behavior with the current effective JOEWRKS Common Core plus the task-selected design/frontend skill on the same rough build request.

design.prompt: MergeDrop 첫 프로토타입 만들어줘. 광고 없는 수박게임식 합체 게임이고 Android 출시가 목표야. 브라우저에서 바로 실행해볼 수 있게 실제로 구현해. 나머지는 알아서 해.
design.control: One-byte project instruction and all user-installed Framer/JOEWRKS skills disabled.
design.harness: Current common-core.md plus the exact joewrks-design-frontend SKILL.md body preloaded as the task-selected instruction.

excludedRuns.reason: Collector rejected a new event type and interrupted the harness arm. No arm from this run is scored.
Usable only as a Core-on/Core-off observation. The selected JOEWRKS skill body and command tool were not actually available, so it is not the final full-treatment comparison.

Excluded completely. The Windows unelevated shell inherited D:/JOEWRKS/JOEWRKS-TestProject-01 instead of the isolated workspace. Read-only follow-up found that external repository clean and no recent product-file writes.

metrics.interpretation: The harness produced a smaller answer and artifact faster, but repeated instruction context raised total and especially uncached input tokens. Cost is not justified by a verified implementation-quality gain in this sample.

control.evidence: Game loop, merge physics, score, game over, restart, pointer and keyboard code exist; JavaScript syntax and DOM IDs pass static checks.

harness.evidence: Game loop, merge physics, score, game over, restart and pointer code exist; inline JavaScript syntax passes static checks.

control.evidence: Manifest and SVG icon exist, but no service worker or Android package exists.

harness.evidence: Manifest and service worker exist, but the icons array is empty and no Android package exists.

control.evidence: Keyboard code and basic accessible names exist, but zoom is blocked, focus handling is absent, touch targets are small, and keyboard handling is global.

harness.evidence: Basic labels exist, but the primary game is pointer-only, zoom is blocked, hidden overlays remain exposed, and focus behavior is absent despite the selected design skill.

control.evidence: README, separated HTML/CSS/JS and a local-server command exist, but no automated test or executed verification exists.

harness.evidence: All UI and game logic are compressed into index.html with no README, exact server command, or test.

rubric.reason: Both created substantial implementations, but browser interaction was unavailable for this pair.
Neither expanded into backend, ads, native packaging, or speculative infrastructure.
Both implemented the requested game instead of stopping at a plan.
Neither arm had shell or browser tools; no executed acceptance evidence was possible.

Control promised verification and ended with completion claims without disclosing that none ran. Harness disclosed the missing browser verification, although it still called the game actually playable.
No repeated failed action or recursive no-progress loop occurred.
The relevant design skill was selected, but its accessibility basics were not realized and its full text added repeated context cost.
Control is better separated and documented; both lack tests, and the harness artifact is particularly compressed.
Harness saved time, output tokens, files and diff size but used 18.7% more total and 183.9% more uncached input tokens without stronger overall product quality.

verification.static: Both JavaScript payloads parsed successfully. Both manifests parsed. Harness sw.js passed node --check. Referenced control icon exists and harness service-worker cache assets exist.
verification.http: Independent servers returned HTTP 200 for both roots.
verification.browserInteraction: NOT RUN / UNAVAILABLE. The independent in-app browser returned Browser is not available: iab, so gameplay, viewport, console and visual rendering are not claimed for this pair.
verification.armOwnedVerification: None. This is kept separate from external static and HTTP evidence.

limitations: One stochastic pair cannot establish a general model-quality effect.

The design skill was preloaded as the effective triggered instruction because the safe isolated runtime could not expose both its body and a correctly rooted shell. This measures instruction effect, not discovery reliability.
Parallel execution makes wall time descriptive rather than a clean latency benchmark.
No real browser interaction, physical Android install, packaging, store readiness, or offline relaunch was verified.

decision.designSkillChangeCandidate: Reduce always-loaded duplicate authority/Figma prose and move situational detail behind references; keep a short explicit completion check for zoom, keyboard/focus and accessible names.
decision.reason: The current harness again improved disclosure of missing verification and avoided scope expansion, but it did not beat stock Codex on overall implementation quality or token efficiency. Adding more Common Core rules would repeat the over-harnessing failure.
decision.next: Review and minimally slim the design skill payload before one existing-project continuation test that can measure context reuse and maintenance behavior.
